title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood serving performance (latency/throughput) vs their current baseline provider. Discussed tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization), identified variance on 99p latency for long-context workloads, agreed next steps: run 10K-request tail-run, share raw perf logs, try dedicated instance with pinned quant profile, schedule on-prem security follow-up.
action_items: Monica Ruiz | Share raw perf logs + flame graphs from Redwood runs | 2025-10-10
Marcus Lee | Provide baseline provider test config + seq length distribution export | 2025-10-10
Liam Carter | Spin up dedicated pinned-quant profile and run 10k tail run; share results | 2025-10-15
Sara Chen | Supply canonical prompt set (50) for quality check vs quantized model | 2025-10-12
next_steps: Redwood to run 10k-request tail benchmark on dedicated pool (pinned quant) and send raw logs
Atlas to export baseline provider config and seq-length histogram
Schedule security deep-dive next week for VPC/KMS questions
Plan short demo on canary rollout + automatic fallback policies
header:
Date: 2025-10-08 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Monica Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sara Chen (Atlas - Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Atlas - Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Atlas - CTO)
transcript:
[00:00:03] Liam Carter: hey everyone thanks for joining on time um we can start, quick agenda — benchmark numbers from this week, tuning notes, and next steps.
[00:00:12] Sara Chen: yep thanks liam, excited to see the numbers. we've been seeing pretty high tail latency on our baseline so hoping to compare.
[00:00:27] Monica Ruiz: ok i'll kick off with the summary of the runs we did thursday, so to recap we ran the same 5000 request suite against your baseline (internal provider) and against Redwood hosted-optimized and then a small run on a dedicated pool with pinned quantization. results are in the sheet i shared.
[00:00:45] Marcus Lee: quick note, baseline was running on our on-prem cluster (A100s) with their default batching config, no kv cache enabled,/
[00:00:52] Marcus Lee: — sorry no KV cash enabled, i said cash earlier lol.
[00:00:59] Monica Ruiz: no worries. so headline numbers: median token latency on Redwood hosted was slightly better, about 8% lower than baseline; throughput was comparable. however 99p latency for long-context (2.5k tokens) spiked on our hosted runs to ~1.8s per token vs baseline 1.3s per token.
[00:01:20] Sara Chen: that's the thing we care about — our user flows hit those long contexts and tail latency kills UX.
[00:01:27] Monica Ruiz: yeah. digging in, we saw two main contributors: kv cache warmup and attention kernel selection for long sequences. on the dedicated pinned-quant run we did see the 99p come down to ~1.5s per token, so an improvement but still not quite baseline.
[00:01:45] Priya Nair: was there any difference in quality when you pinned quant? did you run the sample prompts?
[00:01:52] Monica Ruiz: we did a small quality spot check — about 50 prompts — and saw minor delta in output where the quantized model softened some rare tokens, nothing catastrophic but we flagged 3 prompts for deeper eval. sara, you mentioned you'll share canonical prompt set?
[00:02:08] Sara Chen: yes i'll upload a canonical set by monday.
[00:02:14] Liam Carter: couple of clarifying q's — Marcus, can you confirm the baseline provider's batching window and whether they used micro-batching? helps us line up configs.
[00:02:25] Marcus Lee: baseline used a 20ms batching window and micro-batching on 4 request groups. we can export the config.
[00:02:33] Monica Ruiz: ok thanks. one thing we noticed is our default continuous batching policy is more aggressive which helps throughput but can widen tail. we can tweak to a more latency-sensitive policy (lower batch windows) for these flows.
[00:02:47] [00:02:47] Monica Ruiz: also the KV cache hit ratio on the hosted runs was 68% for these traces; on dedicated it jumped to 82% which explains part of the reduction.
[00:03:02] Sara Chen: why would KV hit ratio differ between hosted and dedicated? same request set, right?
[00:03:09] Monica Ruiz: same request set but different cache placement and instance reuse patterns — hosted has more multi-tenancy, so cold starts and eviction rates are slightly higher under load. on dedicated we bind long-lived workers which preserves the KV entries longer.
[00:03:23] Marcus Lee: makes sense. could we simulate the dedicated worker lifetime in hosted for a test?
[00:03:28] Monica Ruiz: we can approximate by increasing worker pinning, yes. we'll run a pinned-worker hosted run as a config.
[00:03:34] Sara Chen: another question — did you use Redwood's autobalance routing? we want to avoid cross-region surprises.
[00:03:41] Liam Carter: for these runs we pinned region to us-east-1 to keep consistent. good call though, routing can add variance.
[00:03:53] [00:04:00] Monica Ruiz: i want to call out that the attention kernel choice for long sequences can flip depending on seq len and hardware. sometimes the runtime picks a fallback kernel for 2k+ that is slower. we have a tuning knob to prefer the faster kernel at some memory cost, want to try that for your dedicated runs?
[00:04:16] Priya Nair: what's the memory tradeoff? we are constrained on memory for other services.
[00:04:21] Monica Ruiz: it costs about 10-15% more GPU memory headroom per worker, rough numbers. on our dedicated pool we had the headroom, on your hosted tests if you want that we'll need slightly bigger instance shape.
[00:04:33] Marcus Lee: hmm we might be ok if it buys down tail.
[00:04:37] Sara Chen: any smart caching ideas? we have a lot of repeated prefixes.
[00:04:42] Monica Ruiz: yes we can enable prefix caching more aggressively; there's also an LRU window you can tune. i think with your workload prefix reuse we could push cache hit to mid 90s.
[00:04:52] Sara Chen: that would be huge.
[00:04:55] Liam Carter: high level tradeoff summary: dedicated + pinned quant + kernel preference + aggressive prefix caching = best tail numbers but costs more; hosted with tuning (lower batch windows, pinned workers) may approach baseline but multi-tenancy eviction remains a small source of noise.
[00:05:12] [00:05:20] Monica Ruiz: quick aside on quantization: we used int4 pinned quant for the dedicated test; quality delta was small on most prompts but for some rare token distributions it changed. we can do mixed-precision on the hot layers to mitigate — that's what our optimize tool recommends.
[00:05:36] Sara Chen: ok can you share the optimize recommendations?
[00:05:40] Monica Ruiz: yes i'll export the optimize report after the call.
[00:05:45] Marcus Lee: for the 99p numbers can you share the per-request breakdown? sample outliers?
[00:05:51] Monica Ruiz: yes we'll include the tail-run logs and flame graphs. note that the 2.5k sequence runs had a small set of requests that hit disk for kv eviction which spiked.
[00:06:05] Priya Nair: do you have any SLA guarantees on that dedicated config?
[00:06:10] Liam Carter: for Dedicated we offer an SLA-backed latency target per contract, we can propose targets in the SOW once we know the committed capacity.
[00:06:18] Sara Chen: thanks. security question: how are logs stored? we need auditability for regulated workloads.
[00:06:25] Liam Carter: logs can be streamed to your S3, we support customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 docs — monica will follow up with a security pack.
[00:06:36] Monica Ruiz: yep i'll attach the SOC2 and the KMS integration doc.
[00:06:40] [00:06:49] Marcus Lee: quick perf nit — in the shared spreadsheet i noticed a couple of runs with higher variance around minute 32. could be network noise; do you correlate with infra events?
[00:06:58] Monica Ruiz: we saw a small node swap during that window on hosted, which explains some variance. we'll mark those runs as noisy and exclude from the canonical 99p calc.
[00:07:11] Sara Chen: okay good.
[00:07:14] Liam Carter: let's go through specific numbers now, table 2 in the sheet: median token latency — baseline 12ms, redwood hosted 11.1ms, dedicated pinned quant 10.2ms; throughput roughly baseline 180 tokens/s vs redwood hosted 185 tokens/s. 99p for 2.5k: baseline 1.3s, hosted 1.8s (noisy runs included), dedicated 1.5s.
[00:07:43] Monica Ruiz: exact numbers are in the sheet, i'll paste a link in the follow-up.
[00:07:48] Sara Chen: thanks. do you have suggestions on what we should run next?
[00:07:53] Monica Ruiz: recommended next runs: (1) 10k-request tail-run on dedicated pinned-quant with kernel preference and aggressive prefix caching, (2) hosted pinned-worker run to simulate dedicated worker lifetime, (3) quality run of the canonical 50 prompts across quant vs fp16.
[00:08:09] Marcus Lee: we'll take (2) and (3) internally too; for (1) please run and share result logs.
[00:08:15] Liam Carter: timeline: monica can run (1) this week, share logs by friday; sara to upload prompts by monday; marcus to share baseline config by friday.
[00:08:25] [00:08:30] Monica Ruiz: on the topic of canary rollouts — if you want to test traffic split we can show the console demo; it will let you route X% to redwood and fallback to baseline on errors.
[00:08:40] Priya Nair: that sounds useful for staged migration.
[00:08:44] Sara Chen: do you support per-route token cost breakdown? procurement asked for clear unit economics.
[00:08:52] Liam Carter: yes token-level cost and per-route dashboards are available; we'll include sample billing export.
[00:08:59] Marcus Lee: another ask from infra — can we get flame graphs per worker to see where time is spent?
[00:09:06] Monica Ruiz: yes we'll include flame graphs, and also KV hit heatmaps.
[00:09:11] [00:09:20] Sara Chen: any other latency optimization ideas we haven't talked about?
[00:09:24] Monica Ruiz: micro-optimizations: 1) prefix compression for repeated tokens, 2) warm-up runs before production to prepopulate KV, 3) tune the continuous batching policy, 4) experiment with mixed precision on first n layers.
[00:09:39] Sara Chen: nice.
[00:09:41] [00:09:48] Liam Carter: quick pause for scheduling: can we book a security deep-dive next tuesday?
[00:09:54] Sara Chen: tuesday works.
[00:09:57] Priya Nair: prefer morning PST.
[00:10:00] Liam Carter: ok i'll send a calendar invite for tuesday 10am PST and monica will bring the security pack.
[00:10:07] [00:10:20] Monica Ruiz: one more data point — cost estimate: dedicated pinned-quant run is about 25% higher unit GPU cost vs baseline per-token but reduces tail so net user-experience value may outweigh. we'll run a cost delta spreadsheet and share.
[00:10:37] Marcus Lee: we need that for procurement.
[00:10:40] Monica Ruiz: noted.
[00:10:43] [00:18:12] Liam Carter: (lunch break time jump in timestamps — filler to emulate longer call) ok jumping ahead to Q&A — Priya any final concerns?
[00:18:20] Priya Nair: main concern is manageability of dedicated pool and SLO guarantees across traffic spikes; also how rolling upgrades will affect KV cold starts.
[00:18:31] Monica Ruiz: rolling upgrades we do zero-downtime by draining workers — that helps keep KV warm. for burst isolation we can reserve a small burst capacity.
[00:18:41] Sara Chen: what's the minimum commit for Dedicated?
[00:18:45] Liam Carter: typical committed capacity starts at 8 GPUs but flexible based on SOW. we'll put options in the quote.
[00:18:52] [00:19:00] Monica Ruiz: final recap: action items — we'll run the 10k tail, share logs, send security pack, and schedule the deep-dive. thanks everyone for the input.
[00:19:11] Sara Chen: thanks all.
[00:19:15] Marcus Lee: thanks.
[00:19:18] Priya Nair: bye.
[00:19:20] Liam Carter: bye.

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "KV cash") and shorthand. The timestamps are approximate and intended to reflect cadence of meeting.
